about: Real brand names that may not appear on anything sold, branded or labelled in Johansson World. Johansson Studio's checker (src/studio/rules.js) reads it for product, brand and label fields only: story text is not checked, because Orion is also a constellation and Asahi a street here.

copiedFrom.note: That file stays the canonical list for asset kinds and the modeller; this copy adds only what the shop shelves need. Keep the two in step when either changes.

added.orion: jojo's list has only "orion beer", so "Orion lager", "Orion draught" and "Orion, a bottle" slipped through. Orion is a real Okinawan beer.
added.kana: Shelf labels are written in Japanese as often as in English, so the same brands are checked in katakana (and the few written in kanji). Words that are also ordinary words or names here stay out, as in jojo's list: マツダ (also the surname Matsuda) and 日立 (also a city).

leftOut.asahi: Left out on purpose, as in jojo's brandsWhy: Asahi is a street name here.
leftOut.why: Real makers and shops a 1990s Japanese town would show. Words that are also ordinary words or names here are left out on purpose: the onsen's bandai (番台) counter, the Meiji era, Asahi as a street, surnames such as Honda, Suzuki or Toyota, and words like national, sharp, canon or apple.

fields: product.label (every text layer, and every word printed on a picture)

knownIssues.note: The comment says Okinawa in 1997 drinks Orion; it explains the three drinks below.
Minato's draught: "Orion draught, a frosted mug".
Minato's large bottle: "Orion large bottle and a small glass".
Mrs Sato's kitchen line: "opening a bottle of Orion".
The serving label texture prints ORION; buildBeerBottle ("Umineko large bottle") uses that cell, and Mr Fujita's crates use it (world/port-shed.js).
The beer poster already reads UMINEKO, but its red-and-white can recalls Orion's livery.
The red beer poster already reads UMINEKO, but its can recalls Orion's livery.

knownIssuesWhy: World already uses a real brand, Orion. Each use is listed here with its file and line and is printed as a warning (validate, publish_check) until the creator chooses a fictional name; Studio's own fields are refused outright.
